validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: real, correctly classified crude-oil trunk line, confirmed by TWO independent sources, neither GEM-derived. (1) Egypt Oil & Gas trade magazine's special report 'The Western Desert: Egypt's Giant Petroleum Reservoir' (egyptoil-gas.com PDF, created March 2020, drawing on FY2017/18-2018/19 data) has a dedicated 'Crude Oil Infrastructure in the Western Desert' table that names all FOUR El Hamra-linked pipelines as distinct lines: Meleiha-El Hamra (167km/16in/90,000bpd), Badr El Din-El Hamra (128km/12in/60,000bpd), Abu Gharadig-El Hamra (140km/12-16in/60,000bpd) -- and 'El Hamra-Sidi Kerir-Alexandria', From=El Hamra, To=Alexandria, Length=90km, Diameter=16in, Capacity=200,000bpd -- an EXACT match on every value GEM records for this row. The text explains the mechanism: three pipelines deliver Western Desert crude to El Hamra terminal, 'then it is shipped by the fourth pipeline, El Hamra-Sidi Kerir, to refineries in Alexandria'. (url_verifier's automated content check FAILS on this URL because it reads the raw HTTP response as text and cannot decode PDF-stream bytes -- a documented tool limitation for PDFs, not a real content miss; the URL itself is live at HTTP 200, and every value above was confirmed manually via `pdftotext` against the downloaded file.) (2) Independently, the GulfPub PE World Map (registered reference dataset, scraped 2026-02-02) carries ref_id gulfpub:oil:4592, 'Marsa El Hamra - Sidi Kerir', status=Operating, and the reconciliation engine's own route metrics show its drawn endpoints sit only 0.28 km from GEM's own route endpoints for P3693 (endpoint_score 0.946) -- i.e. an independently-scraped, independently-drawn pipeline occupying the identical corridor. Matched at 'yellow' confidence in the committed egypt-oil GulfPub reconciliation run (batches/egypt-oil/staging/recon-gulfpub-20260827/match_diff.json, overlaps). Two GEM-unrelated sources thus independently confirm a real pipeline exists on this exact corridor. DUPLICATE check against the full 46-row Egypt-oil roster: no other row claims El Hamra-to-Sidi Kerir/Alexandria. The three other El Hamra-family rows (P0572 Mleiha-El Hamra, P3689 Badr El Din-El Hamra, P3688 Abu Gharadig-El Hamra) are all INBOUND feeders delivering crude TO El Hamra from producing fields; P3693 is the one OUTBOUND line carrying it onward -- the same EOG source table treats all four as separate lines, so this is not a re-entry of any of them. Also checked against P0530/P5121 (Sumed Oil Pipeline, Ain Sukhna->Alexandria via Sidi Kerir): NOT a duplicate -- Sumed is a completely different physical system (42in twin line, 320km, sourced from Ain Sukhna on the Gulf of Suez, carrying largely imported/transit crude), while P3693 originates at El Hamra in the Western Desert and carries domestically-produced crude; the two pipelines merely arrive in the same general Alexandria/Sidi Kerir refining corridor, which is expected (that is where Egypt's Mediterranean refineries are clustered), not evidence of one row being a re-entry of the other. CLASSIFICATION: Fuel=Oil (crude) is correct -- the EOG source table is explicitly titled 'Crude Oil Infrastructure' and GulfPub separately classifies its matching record under its own 'oil' tracker.

validity.researcher_notes: NEW FINDING (not in the prior pass on this row): while checking whether GulfPub's Capacity=295,000bpd for this row was real corroborating data, I pulled the raw oil source file (sources/gulfpub/data/gulfpub-oil-global.geojson) directly rather than trusting the manifest/match_diff summary, and found `Capacity_Mbpd` is NOT sourced capacity data for the oil dataset -- it is a value derived purely from `diameter`, decoupled from the dataset's own text capacity field. Proof: (1) the raw `capacity` text field is the literal string 'Not specified' on 1,366 of 1,645 oil features (83%), including this exact record (oid 4592); (2) grouping all 1,645 features by `diameter`, the great majority of diameters map to exactly one `Capacity_Mbpd` value tracker-wide (e.g. every diameter=20.0 record, this one included, carries Capacity_Mbpd=295.0; diameter=28.0 -> 579.0; diameter=32.0 -> 756.0; diameter=40.0 -> 1182.0; diameter=48.0 -> 1702.0 -- a few diameters have 2-3 values, consistent with minor data entry noise around an otherwise deterministic diameter->capacity table, not per-pipeline measurement); (3) most conclusively, on the 26 features whose raw `capacity` text DOES state a real figure ('1.4 million barrels per day' -- all on the 'Druzhba'/'Almetievsk-Samara' pipelines, a completely unrelated Russian/European system unrelated to Egypt), `Capacity_Mbpd` still varies purely by that record's own diameter (295.0 for a 20in Druzhba segment, 1702.0 for a 48in one, etc.) and NEVER reflects the stated 1,400 Mbpd -- i.e. the field ignores real reported capacity even when the source itself states one. This is the oil-tracker analogue of the already-documented gas-tracker defect (sources/gulfpub/NOTES.md: '`Capacity_mmcfd` is a constant `300` placeholder ... must never be used as a capacity corroboration'), except worse in practice because it is diameter-varying rather than a flat constant, so it looks like plausible real data to a researcher (and did, in the version of this shard's spec-conflict note written before this check). This is registry-wide, not Egypt- or P3693-specific: `sources/gulfpub/manifest.yml`'s oil dataset column_map still maps `capacity: Capacity_Mbpd` with no caveat, and every committed oil GulfPub reconciliation (at minimum egypt-oil, iraq-oil, saudi-arabia-oil per a repo-wide grep for `Capacity_Mbpd` in batches/) inherits this. I am not editing the shared manifest/NOTES.md myself -- that is a cross-country decision + re-run outside a single-PID validity pass -- but flagging it prominently per the standing 'fix our own defects' rule so it reaches whoever can make that call.

validity.researcher_notes: GEM records Operator='شركة بترول الصحراء الغربية (ويبكو)' -- i.e. Western Desert Petroleum Company (WEPCO). This is a real, well-documented company (operator of El Hamra Terminal since 1968, per its own official 'About Us' page at wepco-eg.com/about-us/, live-verified 2026-08-27), so the entity itself is not fabricated. But whether WEPCO is the OPERATOR OF THIS SPECIFIC 90km/16in export pipeline to Sidi Kerir/Alexandria is a genuinely open question, on two independent signals found this pass: (1) The GulfPub PE World Map's independent record for this exact corridor (gulfpub:oil:4592, route endpoints 0.28km from GEM's own -- see the existence note above) names the operator as 'Petroleum Pipelines Co' (PPC), not WEPCO. (2) WEPCO's own current official website is detailed about what it directly operates -- its 'About Us' page states WEPCO's core operations are 'Onshore shipping to local refineries', 'Offshore export/import ... via tankers', and explicitly 'Managing & Operating WEPCO 12" pipeline' (singular, 12-inch -- not 16in or 20in); its 'El Hamra Terminal' operations page separately describes WEPCO's own marine-loading subsea lines in detail (a 36in/9km SBM line since 2019 and a 30in/7km SBM line) -- and NEITHER page anywhere mentions 'Sidi Kerir' as a place (the only 'Sidi' hit on either page is 'Sidi Gaber', a different Alexandria neighborhood that is part of WEPCO's mailing address) or 'Alexandria' as a shipping destination for a trunk pipeline. The 2020 EOG trade report itself only ties WEPCO to controlling/monitoring crude AT the terminal and cites 'WEPCO's official website' for the general routing description, not for who operates the fourth (outbound) pipeline specifically. Given PPC is Egypt's standard national operator for long-haul crude/product trunk pipelines (already independently confirmed as the operator on this same corridor by a separate scraped dataset), and WEPCO's own current self-description of its pipeline assets does not include this line, I am NOT citing a ref for Operator this pass (leaving it UNRESOLVED) -- GulfPub is an internal registered dataset, not a fetchable/citable URL, and WebSearch quota was exhausted this session before a targeted PPC-vs-WEPCO search could be run on this specific pipeline. This is flagged as attribution concern for Update, not a fix I am making unilaterally.
